dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining

evidence.note: Opening orientation: systematically reads Cargo.toml, stubs, and many test files (ipaddress, servicecidr, storage_lifecycle, watch, pod handlers), deriving the public contract from tests rather than inventing it — strong test-side mining.

Lists /opt/k8s-reference only once, labels it 'Go source'/'primarily Go code', and never returns. The mounted upstream reference — the intended source of truth for hidden-conformance semantics — is effectively abandoned.
Repeated filesystem sweeps for cached/pre-built rusternetes code and hidden solutions — a shortcut hunt, not genuine reference-behavior mining.

Precise contract extraction from tests: confirms /registry/{resource}/{ns}/{name} key shape, derives Storage trait methods, discovers enum variants (KeyUsage) and serde type_->"type" renames — accurate per-crate contract reconstruction.

Semantics (JSON merge-patch, SPDY channel framing, admission logic, controller reconcile_all pattern) are coded from test fixtures and general K8s recollection, never cross-checked against the upstream reference.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's reconstruction of the load-bearing public API from tests, stubs, and manifests is thorough and systematic (types, module paths, serde field names, storage-key shape, dependency graph) — reaching the 8-anchor for the contract half of the dimension. But it consults the upstream v1.35 reference essentially zero times after an initial dismissive glance, coding all semantics from test fixtures and memory, which is below even the 5-anchor's 'consults the reference for the specific component.' The strong contract-from-tests work offset by the near-total absence of reference mining places the observed behavior squarely between the 3 and 8 anchors, at a 5.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Opened with workspace cargo check to assess state, then started at leaf crate `common`, and used `cargo test -p rusternetes-common` (34 provided tests green) as the concrete done-check before explicitly deciding storage was the next logical crate.
Followed DAG to storage next, verified compilation, and step 159 confirms both common+storage compile before moving upward to api-server — deferring dependents until foundations verified.

Decomposed the large api-server crate into internally ordered sub-modules (patch, finalizers, filtering, table, spdy, protobuf, response, admission), each with a compile/test-compile check — sequencing sub-goals within a hard crate.
Repeatedly re-sequenced back down to `common` to add missing types discovered while compiling api-server tests, re-running cargo check each time — living re-sequencing as dependencies surfaced.

Explicitly deferred e2e_workflow_test.rs because it depends on the unimplemented controller-manager, then moved to controller-manager as the next dependency layer; TaskCreate markers at 69/221/440 state dependency-aware milestones.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit dependency-aware plan matching the leaf-to-root spec (common→storage→api-server→controller-manager), with per-crate/per-submodule build-or-test milestones, sub-module sequencing inside api-server, deferral of dependents (e2e test), and re-sequencing back to common when missing types surfaced — squarely the level-8 anchor. It does not reach 10 because the api-server exit check was compilation rather than green provided tests, and the hardest downstream crates (scheduler, kubelet) were never reached or decomposed into checkpointed sub-goals within the observed horizon.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures

evidence.note: The only actual `cargo test` runs, both on rusternetes-common; step 68 reports all 34 tests passing. This is the sole crate driven to green via real tests.
Storage crate verified only via `cargo check -p rusternetes-storage` and `cargo check --workspace`; its provided tests were never run, compile success used as the progress signal.

Long api-server span verified exclusively with `cargo check -p rusternetes-api-server --tests` (compile-only, ~75 checks total across run); step 440 celebrates 'all tests compile flawlessly' as the milestone, never executing them.

Trajectory ends mid controller-manager still in the compile-check loop; no workspace test run, no booting the all-in-one binary, no HTTP/JSON/storage-key semantic checks, no acknowledgment of the hidden conformance suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's verification loop is overwhelmingly `cargo check` as a compile-success proxy (75 checks vs 2 real test runs), with only the common crate ever driven to green through its provided tests. It never ran the prescribed per-crate test commands for storage/api-server/controller-manager, never ran the workspace suite, and showed no attempt to validate real Kubernetes HTTP/JSON semantics or anticipate the hidden conformance suite. This matches anchor 3 (compile success / a subset of passing tests treated as done) and falls short of anchor 5, with no trace of the end-to-end semantic verification described in anchors 8-10.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries

evidence.note: The only genuine test run: cargo test -p rusternetes-common, 34 passed, marked as a milestone. After this the agent essentially never tracks test pass/fail again — it switches entirely to compile-checking.

A sustained, disciplined loop of `cargo check -p rusternetes-common` followed by `cargo check -p rusternetes-api-server --tests` after nearly every shared-crate edit — real regression-watching on a shared crate at the compilation level, maintaining a rough per-test-file build ledger.

Tracks remaining failing test files by name ('only dra_test.rs and endpointslice_handler_test.rs left'; 'all api-server tests compile except e2e_workflow_test blocked on controller-manager') — a roughly-maintained done-vs-remaining list, but purely compile status not test pass counts.
Circular debugging on the EndpointSlice Option<Vec<EndpointPort>> mismatch: repeatedly re-reads the same files confused about the error's source without cleanly recognizing it was going in circles.

Trajectory ends with 5+ crates (scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, cloud-provider, all-in-one) never touched and the full workspace suite never run — no consolidated pass/fail picture across the 100 binaries ever established.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent periodically verifies state and methodically works down a list of failing crates/test files, roughly tracking remaining work — squarely anchor 5. Its consistent re-checking of the shared `common` crate plus api-server tests after edits is genuine regression-watching that reaches toward anchor 8, but the monitoring is almost entirely compilation status rather than the 1,390-test pass/fail ledger this dimension centers on (tests were actually run only once), there are no per-binary pass counts or pass/fail deltas, and one episode (steps 433-437) shows undetected circular debugging. That combination lands it at a solid 5, not higher.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Discovered a falsified assumption (missing workspace deps + no-Cargo.toml-edits rule) and re-derived the storage design around available dependencies instead of forcing it.
Chosen implementation approach (delegating schema generation to a subagent) failed/stalled; agent cleanly abandoned it and built types directly.

Strongest adaptation: recognized Storage trait return-type was wrong from test evidence, called it a structural issue, revised the trait AND propagated the corrected contract (and later error type) across memory.rs/etcd.rs — anchor-8 style propagation.

Repeated duplicate-type collisions resolved at the design level by choosing a single definition and re-exporting (ObjectReference, UserInfo, CSIVolumeSource, HostPathVolumeSource) rather than patching each call site.
Large stretch of reactive single-call-site type fixes (Option<T> vs T, field renames) with repeated rewrites of the same common files — symptom-level patching and notable churn, closer to anchor 3-5.
Persistent EndpointSlice ports mismatch: re-investigated across files repeatedly rather than blindly repeating, showing course-correction impulse though somewhat circular.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently treats compile/test failures as signal and backs out wrong per-crate assumptions (anchor 5), and in the Storage-trait/error-type case and the duplicate-type consolidations it propagated a corrected contract fact across all affected files and shared abstractions (anchor 8 behavior). However, it never established the contract up front, and a large fraction of the trajectory is reactive one-mismatch-at-a-time patching with heavy rewriting of the same files — falling short of the proactive, churn-avoiding re-derivation described at level 10. This places observed behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.

rubric.task_read: A massive long-horizon build: reimplement ten interdependent Rust crates that reconstruct Kubernetes (API types, storage, Axum API server, scheduler, controllers, kubelet, proxy, kubectl, cloud, all-in-one) against a fixed public API, 1,390 provided tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite that punishes fixture-fitting without real K8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, a load-bearing contract that cannot be changed, deep cross-crate dependencies, and a mounted v1.35 upstream reference that is the source of truth. This task demands heavy, sustained, well-sequenced meta-work: a skilled practitioner would mine the reference and stubs hard, build leaf-to-root, verify per-crate against real semantics, and constantly track which of 100 binaries pass.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining
dimensions.description: Reconstructing the load-bearing public API from tests/stubs/manifests and mining the mounted upstream v1.35 reference for behavior, rather than coding from memory.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key format) is fixed and untestable to guess; the hidden conformance suite requires genuine K8s semantics available only from /opt/k8s-reference. Acting blind here guarantees compile failures and semantic misses.

anchors.0: Starts editing crates without reading tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, or the reference tree; invents APIs from memory.
anchors.3: Skims a few test files and a stub; consults the reference occasionally but mostly codes from general K8s recollection.
anchors.5: Reads the tests and stubs for the crate at hand and derives its expected signatures/field names; consults the reference for the specific component being built.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the contract per crate (types, module paths, serde field names, storage-key shape) from tests and cross-checks each against the upstream reference; probes the dependency graph before committing to an order; notes semantics the hidden suite will likely exercise.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven orientation across the whole workspace: maps the full crate contract and cross-crate invariants up front, repeatedly returns to the reference to resolve exact behavior (watches, status subresources, controller reconciliation) rather than approximating, and records discovered contract facts so later crates reuse them instead of re-deriving.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered dependency-respecting sequence of sub-goals, each with a concrete done-check (e.g. a crate's provided tests pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The crates form a dependency DAG; the spec itself prescribes leaf-first (common → storage → api-server → upward). Wrong ordering means churning on higher crates whose foundations shift underneath, wasting enormous effort over a long horizon.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated crates or tries to make everything compile at once with no ordering rationale.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates' with no dependency ordering or per-crate completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-to-root order with per-crate build/test as the milestone for each.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware plan with milestones tied to concrete checks (workspace builds, then per-crate provided-test green), sequencing sub-modules within large crates and deferring dependents until their foundation is verified.
anchors.10: A living, granular milestone hierarchy that respects the true dependency DAG, decomposes the hardest crates (api-server, scheduler, kubelet) into internally ordered checkpoints each with an explicit exit test, and is re-sequenced as dependencies are discovered — sustaining coherent forward motion across all 100 test binaries.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided tests AND designing checks for real K8s semantics the hidden conformance suite will test, rather than assuming green fixtures means done.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns that passing visible fixtures without correct Kubernetes semantics fails the hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count toward score. The agent must verify behavior (camelCase JSON, storage keys, watches, status subresources) against the reference, not just the visible suite.

anchors.0: No verification loop; writes code and assumes it works, or never runs the test suite.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test sporadically; treats compile success or a subset of passing tests as done.
anchors.5: Runs the prescribed per-crate and workspace test commands and iterates until provided tests pass.
anchors.8: Systematically drives each crate's provided tests to green, then validates end-to-end semantics (boots the all-in-one binary, checks HTTP behavior/JSON shape/storage keys against the reference) anticipating the hidden conformance suite; distinguishes counted vs non-counted checks.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: per-crate provided tests, workspace-wide runs, plus self-authored semantic probes (used as diagnostics, not for score) that mirror likely conformance assertions and are cross-checked against upstream behavior — catching semantic gaps that visible fixtures miss and confirming they're fixed before moving on.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, current picture of which crates build, which of the 1,390 tests pass, and where effort is stuck, across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Success requires every non-skipped provided test to pass; with 100 binaries and deep dependencies, losing track means undetected regressions and circular debugging. An accurate done-vs-remaining ledger is what sustains progress.

anchors.0: No awareness of overall state; can't say what passes or what's left; repeats fixed work or misses regressions.
anchors.3: Occasional ad hoc test runs with no consolidated view of remaining failures.
anchors.5: Periodically runs the suite and works down a list of failing crates/tests, roughly tracking remaining work.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of build status and per-binary pass counts, watches for regressions when editing shared crates, and detects when a debugging effort is going in circles.
anchors.10: Continuous, precise progress accounting across the whole workspace: quantified pass/fail deltas per run, early detection of thrashing or a crate that keeps re-breaking downstream tests, and deliberate reprioritization based on that signal — never loses the plot across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising approach when a contract assumption, chosen implementation, or ordering turns out wrong — rather than forcing a falsified design forward.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reconstructing a fixed contract from indirect evidence means assumptions will be wrong (a signature, a serialization detail, an ordering); a large workspace punishes barrelling ahead on a bad assumption. Recognizing and reversing course cheaply is decisive over this horizon.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach without change; ignores contradicting test/compile evidence.
anchors.3: Makes local patches to symptoms but doesn't revise the underlying wrong assumption.
anchors.5: When tests or the compiler reveal a wrong assumption, backs out and adopts a corrected approach for that crate.
anchors.8: Treats compile/test failures and reference discrepancies as signal to revise the design or sequencing, propagating a corrected contract fact to all affected crates rather than patching one call site.
anchors.10: Proactively updates the plan and shared abstractions when reality diverges — recognizes a foundational misunderstanding (e.g. a storage or watch semantic) early, re-derives it from the reference, and cleanly refactors dependents, avoiding both stubborn persistence and needless churn.
